note: The death match is a development benchmark (rulings §5.8, §5.20, §5.22). Every arm runs the same tasks on the same model and is scored by deathmatch.py.

arms.prompt: /curmudgeon:review . (review only; change no files; use the lite tier: critic_run.py begin --tier lite)
arms.note: Curmudgeon's lite tier: one blind reviewer, with Critical and High findings verified (ruling §5.53).

arms.prompt: Review the code in this folder for bugs. For each bug give the file:line, what is wrong, and a concrete input or sequence that makes it fail. Change no files.

/code-review:code-review the change on this branch. There is no GitHub pull request: the change is `git diff main...HEAD` in this folder, so read it with git instead of gh, and print your final review comment here instead of posting it. Change no files.
arms.note: Anthropic's official code-review plugin (code-review-anthropics in the Anthropic directory). It reviews GitHub pull requests; here the task is committed as a branch over an empty base, and the prompt says to read the local diff and print the comment.

arms.prompt: /code-review:code-review Treat this local change as the pull request to review. There is no GitHub pull request, so wherever your steps say to use gh, use git instead: the pull request's diff is `git diff main...HEAD` in this folder. For step 1: the pull request is open, is not a draft, needs review, and has no earlier Claude comment, so continue. Its title is "Add the app" and its description is "Adds this application's code." Then follow steps 2 to 7 exactly as written, launching every agent each step names, and print the step 7 summary here. Post nothing. Change no files.
arms.note: The code-review plugin's best effort (ruling §5.53): the same tools, with the pull-request facts its step 1 checks given in the prompt and an explicit instruction to run every step and launch every agent. Each run's agents_launched shows whether it did.
Claude Code's built-in /code-review command (no plugin). It reviews the working folder and replies with a JSON list of findings, which deathmatch.py reads like any other arm's.

Only with local rules in $SEMGREP_RULES, never the registry (it would send data out). The 24 Oct 2026 run used Semgrep's own published javascript/ and html/ rules (semgrep/semgrep-rules, Semgrep Rules License v1.0), kept outside this repository.

arms.prompt: Use the code-reviewer agent (orchestrator:code-reviewer) to review the code in this folder for defects, and print its review here: each defect with the file:line, what is wrong, and an input or sequence that makes it fail. Change no files.
arms.note: rbenzing/Orchestrator (Apache-2.0), a multi-agent build pipeline; its Code Reviewer agent is the part that reviews, so the arm calls it directly. Its scripts are PowerShell; the 27 Oct 2026 run had no PowerShell in the workspace, so any script step it tried failed. Clone it outside this repository and set DM_ORCH_RBENZING to the clone.

arms.prompt: Use the reviewer agent (orchestrator-agent-plugin:reviewer) to review the change on this branch before merge. There is no GitHub pull request and no order file: the change is `git diff main...HEAD` in this folder, read it with git instead of gh, and the intent is a working app with no bugs. Print its review here, with each problem's file:line. Change no files.
arms.note: BVarvill/orchestrator-agent-plugin (MIT); its reviewer agent does the cold pre-merge review, so the arm calls it on the task committed as a branch. Clone it outside this repository and set DM_ORCH_BVARVILL to the clone.

arms.prompt: Use the code-reviewer agent (orchestrator:code-reviewer) to review the code in this folder for defects, and print its review here: each defect with the file:line, what is wrong, and an input or sequence that makes it fail. Change no files.
arms.note: The same arm with PowerShell 7.5.4 installed in the workspace (pwsh, also linked as powershell.exe) and allowed for its scripts (27 Oct 2026, Ryan's yes). Its agents ask for a launch-process tool that the plugin does not define (an outside Windows tool), so they fall back to Bash.
